arxiv-2107-07570.title: Revealing asymmetrical dust distribution in the inner regions of HD 141569
arxiv-2107-07570.creator: G. Singh, T. Bhowmik, A. Boccaletti, P. Thébault, Q. Kral, J. Milli, J. Mazoyer, E. Pantin, J. Olofsson, R. Boukrouche, E. DiFolco, M. Janson, M. Langlois, A.-L. Maire, A. Vigan, M. Benisty, J.-C. Augereau, C. Perrot, R. Gratton, T. Henning, F. Ménard, E. Rickman, Z. Wahhaj, A. Zurlo, B. Biller, M.
arxiv-2107-07570.description: Abstract Context. The combination of high-contrast imaging with spectroscopy and polarimetry offers a pathway to studying the grain distribution and properties of debris disks in exquisite detail. Here, we focus on the case of a gas-rich debris disk around HD 141569A, which features a multiple-ring morphology first identified with SPHERE in the near-infrared. Aims.

arxiv-2201-06095.title: Doing More with Less: Overcoming Data Scarcity for POI Recommendation via Cross-Region Transfer Journal: TIST Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3511711 CCS: Information systems Location based services CCS: Information systems Data mining
arxiv-2201-06095.creator: Vinayak Gupta, Srikanta Bedathur
arxiv-2201-06095.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vinayak Gupta, Srikanta Bedathur. Variability in social app usage across regions results in a high skew of the quantity and the quality of check-in data collected, which in turn is a challenge for effective location recommender systems. In this paper, we present Axolotl (Automated cross Location-network Transfer Learning), a novel method aimed at transferring location preference models learned in a data-rich region to significantly boost the quality of recommendations in a data-scarce region.

arxiv-2210-06145.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Reconstruct Ancient Mosaics?
arxiv-2210-06145.creator: Fernando Moral-Andrés, Elena Merino-Gómez, Pedro Reviriego, Fabrizio Lombardi
arxiv-2210-06145.description: Abstract A large number of ancient mosaics have not reached us because they have been destroyed by erosion, earthquakes, looting or even used as materials in newer construction. To make things worse, among the small fraction of mosaics that we have been able to recover, many are damaged or incomplete.

arxiv-2312-13979.title: The effectiveness of exoplanets and Brown Dwarfs as sub-GeV Dark Matter detectors
arxiv-2312-13979.creator: and J. Diks
arxiv-2312-13979.description: Abstract In this work we demonstrate that Dark Matter (DM) evaporation severely hinders the effectiveness of exoplanets and Brown Dwarfs as sub-GeV DM probes. Moreover, we find useful analytic closed form approximations for DM capture rates for arbitrary astrophysical objects, valid in four distinct regions in the σ − m X \sigma-m_{X} parameter space.

arxiv-2405-18191.title: Instantons in ϕ 4 {{\phi^{4}}} Theories: Transseries, Virial Theorems and Numerical Aspects
arxiv-2405-18191.creator: Ludovico T. Giorgini, Ulrich D. Jentschura, Enrico M. Malatesta, Tommaso Rizzo, Jean Zinn-Justin
arxiv-2405-18191.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ludovico T. Giorgini, Ulrich D. Jentschura, Enrico M. Malatesta, Tommaso Rizzo, Jean Zinn-Justin. We discuss numerical aspects of instantons in two- and three-dimensional ϕ 4 \phi^{4} theories with an internal O ⁡ ( N ) O(N) symmetry group, the so-called N N -vector model. Combining asymptotic transseries expansions for large argument with convergence acceleration techniques, we obtain high-precision values for certain integrals of the instanton that naturally occur in loop corrections around instanton configurations.

arxiv-2406-02564.title: Two-layer baroclinic turbulence with arbitrary layer depths
arxiv-2406-02564.creator: Gabriel Hadjerci, Basile Gallet
arxiv-2406-02564.description: Abstract While heat transport by baroclinic turbulence in oceans and planetary atmospheres is well described by a two-layer model, the relative depth of the two layers varies greatly depending on the situation of interest, making it an important parameter governing the transport properties of the system.

arxiv-2408-16530.title: A Comprehensive Review of 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving: Technological Advances and Future Directions
arxiv-2408-16530.creator: Yu Wang, Shaohua Wang, Yicheng Li, Mingchun Liu
arxiv-2408-16530.description: Abstract In recent years, 3D object perception has become a crucial component in the development of autonomous driving systems, providing essential environmental awareness. However, as perception tasks in autonomous driving evolve, their variants have increased, leading to diverse insights from industry and academia.

arxiv-2411-04827.title: Quantum-Centric Study of Methylene Singlet and Triplet States
arxiv-2411-04827.creator: Ieva Liepuoniute*, Kirstin D. Doney, Javier Robledo Moreno, Joshua A. Job, Will S. Friend, Gavin O. Jones
arxiv-2411-04827.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ieva Liepuoniute*, Kirstin D. Doney, Javier Robledo Moreno, Joshua A. Job, Will S. Friend, Gavin O. Jones. This study explores the electronic structure of the CH 2 molecule, modeled as a (6e, 23o) system using a 52-qubit quantum experiment, which is relevant for interstellar and combustion chemistry. We focused on calculating the dissociation energies for CH 2 in the ground state triplet and the first excited state singlet, applying the Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) method within a quantum-centric supercomputing framework.

arxiv-2504-05571.title: Knowledge-Instruct: Effective Continual Pre-training from Limited Data using Instructions
arxiv-2504-05571.creator: Oded Ovadia, Meni Brief, Rachel Lemberg, Eitam Sheetrit
arxiv-2504-05571.description: Abstract While Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire vast knowledge during pre-training, they often lack domain-specific, new, or niche information. Continual pre-training (CPT) attempts to address this gap but suffers from catastrophic forgetting and inefficiencies in low-data regimes. We introduce Knowledge-Instruct , a novel approach to efficiently inject knowledge from limited corpora through pure instruction-tuning.

arxiv-2507-01855.title: The TESS Grand Unified Hot Jupiter Survey. III. Thirty More Giant Planets. This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 meter Magellan Telescopes located at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile
arxiv-2507-01855.creator: Samuel W. Yee, Joshua N. Winn, Joel D. Hartman, Joseph E. Rodriguez, George Zhou, David W. Latham, Samuel N. Quinn, Allyson Bieryla, Karen A. Collins, Jason D. Eastman, Kevin I. Collins, Dennis M. Conti, Eric L. N. Jensen, David R. Anderson, Özgür Baştürk, David Baker, Khalid Barkaoui, Matthew P. Ba
arxiv-2507-01855.description: Abstract We present the discovery of 1 transiting giant planets that were initially detected using data from NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. These new planets orbit relatively bright ( G ≤ 12.5 G\leq 12.5 ) FGK host stars with orbital periods between 1.6 and 8.2 days, and have radii between 0.9 and 1.7 Jupiter radii.

arxiv-2507-16785.title: The ranks of twists of an elliptic curve in characteristic 3 3
arxiv-2507-16785.creator: João Paulo Guardieiro
arxiv-2507-16785.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by João Paulo Guardieiro. Abstract Starting from the elliptic curve E:y^{2}=x^{3}-x over \mathbb{F}_{9} , a curve \mathcal{X} over \mathbb{F}_{3^{2n}} and a cyclic cover of \mathcal{X} of degree m\in\{2,3,4,6\} , we construct the corresponding m -twists over the function field \mathbb{F}_{3^{2n}}(\mathcal{X}) . We also obtain the Mordell-Weil rank of these twists in terms of the Zeta functions of \mathcal{X} and of suitable Kummer and Artin-Schreier extensions of it.

arxiv-2512-17421.title: Rydberg Atomic RF Sensor-based Quantum Radar Thanks: This paper has been accepted for presentation at the IEEE Applied Sensing Conference (APSCON 2026). This work was supported in part by the INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship (Reg. No.: IFA22-ENG 344), ANRF Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant (ANRF/
arxiv-2512-17421.creator: Sourav Banerjee and Neel Kanth Kundu
arxiv-2512-17421.description: Abstract Rydberg atom-based RF sensors offer distinct advantages over conventional dipole antennas for electric field detection. This paper presents a system model and performance analysis of a Rydberg atom-based quantum radar, which employs optical readout via lasers and photon detectors instead of circuit-based receivers.

pmc-11301949.title: Public involvement in an aggregate and individual participant data meta-analysis of mindfulness-based programmes for mental health promotion
pmc-11301949.creator: Claire Friedrich, Toni Fairbairn, Graham Denton, Mary Geddes, Darren Thomas-Carr, Peter B Jones, Julieta Galante
pmc-11301949.description: BackgroundInvolving the public in evidence synthesis research is challenging due to the highly analytic nature of the projects, so it is important that involvement processes are documented, reflected upon, and shared to devise best practices. There is a literature gap on the involvement of the public in individual participant data meta-analyses, particularly in public health projects.

pmc-11336738.title: Noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis in mini pigs using an 18F–AlF-NOTA-RGD2 PET/CT molecular probe
pmc-11336738.creator: Wenrui Liu, Hongwei Xu, Haili Zhang, Maodi Xie, Yundi Liu, Li Wang, Xiaoai Wu, Yinrui Feng, Kefei Chen
pmc-11336738.description: To evaluate the efficacy of the 18F–AlF-NOTA-RGD2 positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) molecular probe for the noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis in mini pigs, a potential alternative to invasive diagnostic methods was revealed. This study used 18F–AlF-NOTA-RGD2 PET/CT imaging of mini pigs to assess liver fibrosis.

pmc-11430948.title: Prospective Evaluation of Transsphenoidal Pituitary Surgery in Patients with Cushing’s Disease: Delayed Remission and the Role of Postsurgical Cortisol as a Predictive Factor
pmc-11430948.creator: Athanasios Saratziotis, Maria Baldovin, Claudia Zanotti, Sara Munari, Diego Cazzador, Enrico Alexandre, Luca Denaro, Jiannis Hajiioannou, Enzo Emanuelli
pmc-11430948.description: Background. Transsphenoidal surgery is the treatment of choice for Cushing’s disease. Successful surgery is associated with subnormal postoperative serum cortisol concentrations and cortisoluria levels, which may guide decisions regarding immediate reoperation. Remission is defined as the biochemical reversal of hypercortisolism with the re-emergence of diurnal circadian rhythm. Methods.

pmc-11484994.title: RadioComics—Santa Claus and the breakthrough reaction
pmc-11484994.creator: Paolo Lombardo, Knud Nairz, Ingrid Boehm
pmc-11484994.description: Graphical Abstract Image-guided examinations are required by all medical disciplines and for a majority of patients [1]. Many imaging challenges need to be enhanced, and every year, several 100 million doses of contrast media (iodinated > gadolinium-based) are applied worldwide.

pmc-11689447.title: ABUSE ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE: CONNECTIONS WITH ELDER ABUSE
pmc-11689447.creator: Julie Miller, Lori Mars
pmc-11689447.description: Likely conservative estimates suggest that 1 in every 10 Americans aged 60+ have experienced some form of elder abuse. As theoretical understandings of abuse in general have evolved, so too have conceptualizations of abuse at different stages of the life course, including in older adulthood.

pmc-11728298.title: Fabricating a SFMA/BAChol/PAA/ZnCl2 Hydrogel with Excellent Versatile Comprehensive Properties and Stable Sensitive Freezing-Tolerant Conductivity for Wearable Sensors
pmc-11728298.creator: Jie-Ping Fan, Ming-Ru Xie, Chao Yuan, Jia Ma, Ke-Pu Fu, Chun-Hong Huang, Hui-Ping Chen, Hai-Long Peng, Chun-Fang Xie
pmc-11728298.description: Flexible wearable sensors have obtained tremendous interest in various fields and conductive hydrogels are a promising candidate. Nevertheless, the insufficient mechanical properties, the low electrical conductivity and sensitivity, and the limited functional properties prevent the development of hydrogels as wearable sensors. In this study, an SFMA/BAChol/PAA/ZnCl2 hydrogel was fabricated with high mechanical strength and versatile comprehensive properties.

pmc-12575600.title: The use of diagnostic tools to assess the risks of chemicals to freshwater ecosystems: towards a unified evaluation framework
pmc-12575600.creator: Andreu Rico, Udo Hommen, Beate I. Escher, Alina Koch, Anne Bado-Nilles, Belén González-Gaya, Enya Cody, Francisco Sylvester, Gabriele Treu, Gastón Alurralde, Henner Hollert, Iker Alvarez-Mora, S. Jannicke Moe, Joanne de Jonge, Kelsey Ng, Manu Soto, Matthias Liess, Melis Muz, Mirco Bundschuh, Naroa L
pmc-12575600.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The risk assessment of chemicals relies on multiple tools to quantify the ecological responses of ecosystems to existing chemical pollution. These tools are broadly categorized into three major groups: toxic pressure assessments, bioassays, and ecological monitoring. Here, we examine the strengths and limitations of these approaches, their current level of implementation for freshwater ecosystems across Europe, and their ability to evaluate the impacts of chemicals under field conditions.

pmc-12623871.title: The Amerigo Vespucci as a traveling laboratory for studying the cosmic-ray fluxes at sea level
pmc-12623871.creator: Davide Cerasole, Federica Cuna, Gaia De Palma, Riccardo Di Tria, Leonardo Di Venere, Fabio Gargano, Mario Giliberti, Francesco Licciulli, Antonio Liguori, Pierpaolo Loizzo, Francesco Loparco, Leonarda Lorusso, Mario Nicola Mazziotta, Giuliana Panzarini, Roberta Pillera, Davide Serini
pmc-12623871.description: We have installed and operated a plastic scintillator detector counter to measure the flux of cosmic radiation during the 2023−2025 tour of the historical vessel Amerigo Vespucci. The Vespucci is the oldest ship of the Italian Navy and serves as a training vessel for Navy cadets.

pmc-12688494.title: Diagnostic value of pleural fluid carbohydrate antigen 242 for malignant pleural effusion
pmc-12688494.creator: Xi Lin, Yan Niu, Jian-Xun Wen, Mei Li, Wen-Qi Zheng, Li Yan, Ran-Tong Bao, Zhi-De Hu, Man Zhang, Ya-Nan Xu
pmc-12688494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCarbohydrate antigen 242 (CA242) shows potential as a tumor marker in the diagnosis of malignant pleural effusion (MPE). However, previous studies have been limited by small sample sizes and a narrow range of etiological types.

pmc-13439071.title: PSCSE: prompt-based contrastive learning with sample filtering for unsupervised sentence embedding
pmc-13439071.creator: Biao Li, Xuebing Yang, LiPing Xie
pmc-13439071.description: Unsupervised sentence representation learning is critical in natural language processing. Recently, contrastive learning methods achieved remarkable performance by optimizing the alignment and uniformity of embedding spaces. Nevertheless, the dominant methods mainly focus on the data augmentation for the positive samples but ignore the sampling approach for the negative samples.

uslaw-usc-t7-s2218.title: 7 U.S.C. § 2218 — Fee for administering or taking oaths, affirmations, and affidavits
uslaw-usc-t7-s2218.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t7-s2218.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 55 (Department Of Agriculture). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. No officer, agent, or employee of the Department of Agriculture shall demand or accept any fee or compensation whatsoever for administering or taking any oath, affirmation, or affidavit under the authority conferred by section 2217 of this title.
